source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 289 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 289.

PD 289.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 289 was established by Ordinance No. 19864, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 24, 1988. Ordinance No. 19864 amended Ordinance Nos. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 289 is established on property generally located along the east line of Dallas Parkway, south of the south line of Spring Valley Road. The size of PD 289 is approximately 4.215 acres. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the interpretations in Chapter 51 apply to this article.

(b) All references and definitions in this article refer to Chapter 51. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Dallas Parkway Center Study
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.104. DALLAS PARKWAY CENTER STUDY.

The Dallas Parkway Center Study is a land use study adopted by the city council on June 26, 1985, which addresses, among other things, problems of density and transportation in an area bounded by Interstate Highway 635, Montfort Drive, the Dallas North Tollway, and Belt Line Road. A copy of the adopted study is on file in the department of development services. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Conceptual Site Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.105. CONCEPTUAL SITE PLAN.

Development of the Property must comply with the conceptual site plan (Exhibit 289A). (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Development And Landscape Plans
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.106. DEVELOPMENT AND LANDSCAPE PLANS.

A development plan for each phase of development must be submitted to the city plan commission for approval prior to the issuance of a building permit for any work within that phase. Within one year of February 24, 1988, an initial development plan must be submitted to the city plan commission for approval. Each development plan must be accompanied by a landscape plan which must also be approved by the city plan commission. All development must comply with the approved development and landscape plans. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Permitted Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.107. PERMITTED USES.

The only uses permitted on the Property are those uses permitted in an SC Shopping Center District. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Office Uses Defined
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.108. OFFICE USES DEFINED.

For the purposes of this article, unless otherwise stated, office uses include office, medical clinic, and bank or savings and loan office uses. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Building Setbacks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.109. BUILDING SETBACKS.

Minimum building setbacks are as follows:

(1) Twenty-five feet from the existing south right-of-way line of Spring Valley Road.

(2) Twenty-five feet from the existing east right-of-way line of the Dallas North Tollway service road.

(3) Twenty-eight feet from the south property line.

(4) No minimum setback along the property boundary abutting City Block A/7007, as shown on the conceptual site plan.

(5) No minimum setback along the east property line.

(6) Any below-grade structure that is within 28 feet of the south property line or is within 10 feet of the existing south right-of-way line of Spring Valley Road, or is within 10 feet of the existing east right-of-way line of the Dallas North Tollway service road, must be approved by the director of public works and transportation as not interfering with the purposes of the surface easements for street purposes to be dedicated pursuant to Section 51P-289.115. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Coverage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.110. MAXIMUM COVERAGE.

Maximum permitted coverage of the Property, including aboveground parking structures, is 80 percent. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Floor Area
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.111. MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA.

Maximum total floor area for each use category is shown on the following chart:

Use Category Square Feet

Office 398,101 Hotel 209,527 Retail, bar and restaurant, and private recreation (retail-related) uses 33,981 (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Bonus, Conversion, And Phasing
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.112. BONUS, CONVERSION, AND PHASING.

In conjunction with the provisions of Section 51P-289.110, the following bonus, conversion, and phasing regulations may be applied.

(1) An additional 31,429 square feet of office floor area may be constructed when all of the following three events have occurred:

(A) Transfer stations for DART buses are completed and operational:

(i) within one-half mile of the Dallas North Tollway and Arapaho Road intersection; and

(ii) within one-half mile of the Noel Road and I-635 intersection.

(B) An internal circulation bus system service as described in the Dallas Parkway Center Study for “initial” and “intermediate years” is in operation, as determined by the director of public works and transportation.

(C) The Noel Road and I-635 ramp connections as described in the Dallas Parkway Center Study are constructed, or December 31, 1990, whichever first occurs.

(2) Up to 209,527 square feet of office floor area may be converted to additional retail-related floor area, at a ratio of three square feet of office to one square foot of retail-related floor area.

(3) Up to 10,476 square feet of retail-related floor area may be converted to additional office floor area, at a ratio of two square feet of office to one square foot of retail-related floor area.

(4) Up to 19,094 additional square feet for any use permitted in the SC Shopping Center District may be transferred to the Property from the Texas Turnpike Authority property abutting the Property to the west, in accordance with City Ordinance No. 18214.

(5) Up to 209,527 square feet of hotel floor area may be converted to an additional 91,898 square feet of office floor area at a ratio of 2.28 square feet of hotel to one square foot of office. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Maximum Permitted Height
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.113. MAXIMUM PERMITTED HEIGHT.

Maximum permitted height for any structure is 240 feet above-grade. All structures that exceed 163 feet above-grade must be approved by the Federal Aviation Administration as not hazardous to air navigation prior to issuance of a building permit. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.114. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) Phased office parking limit.

(1) In order to promote the development of transportation alternatives, maximum number of parking spaces for office uses on the Property is restricted in accordance with the regulations below. In order to permit adequate parking for initial phases of development, the restrictions are phased to

gradually reduce the ratio of parking spaces to office floor area from 3.0 spaces for each 1,000 square feet to 2.38 for each 1,000 square feet as development progresses. For the purposes of this phased office parking list, “office use” does not include medical clinics.

(2) Maximum number of parking spaces for office use is 3.0 spaces per 1,000 square feet until building permits have been issued for construction of 237,964 square feet of office use. When building permits have been issued for construction of more than 237,964 square feet of office use, but less than 297,455 square feet, maximum number of parking spaces is 2.5 spaces per 1,000 square feet of office use. Maximum number of parking spaces for office use when building permits have been issued for construction of more than 297,455 square feet of office use is 2.38 spaces per 1,000 square feet.

(b) Minimum office parking. Minimum permissible number of parking spaces provided for office use at any stage of development is 2.0 spaces per 1,000 square feet.

(c) Requirements for other uses. All uses other than office must supply parking in compliance with the minimum requirements of the Dallas Development Code; however, no off-street parking may be supplied in excess of the requirements of the Dallas Development Code. The provisions of Section 51-4.301(c)(6) (the mixed use parking reduction bonus) do not act to restrict the maximum number of spaces permitted, but may be used to calculate the minimum number of spaces permitted.

(d) No parking signs. “No parking signs” must be provided by the owner on all dedicated streets traversing or bordering the Property at the direction of the director of the department of public works and transportation.

(e) Location of parking spaces. No off-street parking spaces at grade, or above or below- grade parking structures within 8.5 feet of grade are permitted within 10 feet of the back of the projected street curb lines along the Tollway Service Road and Spring Valley Road. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Street Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.115. STREET IMPROVEMENTS.

The owner(s) must dedicate all street right-of-way indicated on the conceptual site plan within 90 days of receiving notice from the director of public works and transportation that the city is preparing to begin utility or paving operations or prior to issuance of any building permit, which ever is first. The right-of-way may be dedicated in fee simple or as an easement for street purposes. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.116. ACCESS.

Curb cuts for vehicular ingress-egress are limited to the number and approximate locations shown on the conceptual site plan. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.117. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided below, all signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning district contained in the Dallas Development Code.

(b) Only one electronic non-premise sign is permitted on the Dallas Parkway frontage.

(c) Those signs in place on February 24, 1988, must be removed or relocated on the Property within 90 days of the date of notification from the director of public works and transportation that the

right-of-way must be cleared for street construction. These signs must be removed before more than 228,219 square feet are certified to be occupied on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Transportation Systems Management
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.118. TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS MANAGEMENT.

(a) Generally. The owner(s) shall establish and operate a Transportation Systems Management (TSM) program to encourage carpool, vanpool, and other transit alternatives. A specific TSM action program must be submitted to the city, concurrently with the submission of the first development plan submitted for office use in excess of 10,000 square feet. An annual report must be furnished to the director of public works and transportation.

(b) Reports. The first report must be submitted within two years after the issuance of the first certificate of occupancy on the Property for office use in excess of 10,000 square feet and must be submitted annually thereafter until directed otherwise by the director of public works and transportation. The final report must be submitted two years after the issuance of the certificate of occupancy which would permit occupancy of 90 percent of the final building shown on the development plan(s).

(c) Alternative. In lieu of the requirements in Subsection (a), the owner(s) may participate in and fund, on a pro rata basis with other local area property owners, an area-wide Transportation Management Organization (TMO) that is approved by the city. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Mandatory      Transportation                          Management
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.119. MANDATORY TRANSPORTATION MANAGEMENT ORGANIZATION SUPPORT FEE.

(a) General. Prior to the issuance of the building permit for construction of a building for office use, the owner(s) must pay to the director of public works and transportation a fee of $.05 per square foot of office use for which a building permit is sought. The fees collected under this article must be used for the establishment and operation of an area-wide Transportation Management Organization
(TMO) for the area described in the Dallas Parkway Center Study. The fee must be adjusted annually, using 1986 as the base year, to reflect changes in service costs by using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPIU) for the Dallas/Fort Worth Standard Metropolitan Statistical Area.

(b) Refund. If, after a period of five years from the time of payment of a TMO fee, at least 80 percent of the interest earned has not been spent by transfer, allocation, or any other method for TMO operations, based on a first-in/first-out accounting method, the fee paid will be refunded to the payor or his assignee, together with any remaining interest accrued at the city’s investment rate, upon his allocation for refund, which must include proof of the amount and time of payment. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.120. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

Development of the Property within this PD must comply with the requirements of all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.121. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.122. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-289.123. ZONING MAP.

PD 289 is located on Zoning Map No. C-7. (Ord. Nos. 19864; 25711)
